messages:
sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC tweak there are a couple of failing SCIM provisions for a customer org. Getting 403s from the SCIM endpoint and KMS decrypt logs show `Decrypt failed: invalid ciphertext` for the service-account key. Also noticed SAML audit events with NameID values that don't match the SCIM externalId mapping. Anyone else seeing this?

clair: @sam I saw one alert in the SSO relay. Which customer/org? can you paste the assertion sample (obfuscated) and the SCIM payload?

sam: Org: acme-internal-prod. Quick paste (sanitized):
```
SAML Assertion: Issuer: https://idp.acme.com
NameID: "user+alias@acme.com"
Attributes: email=user@acme.com, uid=12345
```
SCIM POST to /Users returns 403 with body: `\{"detail\":\"KMS decryption failure\",\"status\":403\}`

jyoti: Two things to triage: 1) RBAC change yesterday removed the old "allow-scim-service" role for the dedicated-service-account? 2) KMS IAM policy rotation may have dropped decrypt perms for the service principal. If NameID != externalId we might be double-creating or hitting a uniqueness check and then KMS tries to decrypt the cached token.

idp-bot: Automated: detected SAML audience mismatch for issuer https://idp.acme.com at 2024-10-12T18:22:11Z. Assertion NameID differs from SCIM externalId for 8 events in the past hour.

ops-oncall: I'm on it. I'll check the service-account roles and KMS key policy. If we lost kms:Decrypt on the node group principal we'll see exactly that error. @mike can you grab the key alias and policy?

mike: Key alias: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/redwood/cryptoKeys/scim-key. Policy shows principals: `serviceAccount:scim-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `serviceAccount:old-scim@...` — I see the old-scim SA was removed in the RBAC rollback but we didn't add the new runner yet. That explains the decrypt failures.

clair: Ok that explains KMS 403. But what about the NameID mismatch? Are we trusting NameID for externalId mapping still? we changed to prefer `uid` in SCIM mapping a while back.

sam: Our SCIM connector does: externalId = SAML.NameID if present else Attributes.uid. The customer updated their IdP to send email-like NameIDs for alias addresses. That caused duplicate-checks because email alias != canonical uid and we try to provision, then deprovision flow hits KMS-decrypt of old envelope key.

jyoti: Mitigation plan: 1) Restore kms:Decrypt for scim-runner short-term (ops). 2) Roll a small config tweak to SCIM mapping to normalize NameID -> use `uid` claim when present and fall back to email. 3) Add a validation step in provisioning to avoid attempting decrypt of non-existent envelope keys (idempotency). 4) Notify customer to revert IdP NameID change or add `uid` claim.

ops-oncall: Restored decrypt perms for scim-runner at 18:30 UTC, I also temporarily added back the old service account mapping to the key while we do the config change. SCIM requests are starting to succeed for previously-failing users.

mike: I'll open a quick PR to update the key IAM to include the canonical scim-runner and add a short expiry invite to rotate the old account.

clair: I'll patch the SCIM mapping in staging to prefer `uid` and add a small e2e test for NameID variations. Can we also add an audit alert for when `SAML.NameID != attribute.uid` to catch this earlier?

sam: Yes please. Also raising a vuln-triage note: this behavior allowed a timing window where orphaned encrypted blobs were referenced without proper guards — we should log and handle it as soft-fail instead of hard 403 in the service layer. Filing a follow-up ticket.

jyoti: I'll take ownership of the follow-up: add enhanced logging + idempotency check + test cases for NameID permutations. Repro steps look straightforward.

sam: Thanks all — marking as resolved in-thread since ops restored decrypt and provisioning backfilled. Will circulate a short postmortem with steps and customer comms. :thumbsup:
